# Task: device responsiveness probe for the hardware engine

You are working in the ModernWigiDash repository (a .NET 10 solution,
ModernWigiDash.slnx). Scope of this task: ModernWigiDash.App/ and
ModernWigiDash.Hardware/ (plus ModernWigiDash.Tests/ for the tests). Never
touch files in any other project, and skip obj/ and bin/.

Background: the USB status badge (the `UsbStatus` text, fed from the
engine's connection state) only reports the connection machine
(Disconnected/Connecting/Connected/Simulated). A wedged device (observed
in the field: a force-killed app can wedge the display's bulk pipe) leaves
the engine Connected while frame sends silently fail. Add a lightweight
device responsiveness probe so the App can notice this at the 1-second
telemetry cadence.

Requirements:

1. Engine (ModernWigiDash.Hardware): add a method to
   `DisplayDeviceEngine` that performs one responsiveness check through
   the existing transport: issue the vendor wake command (0x12 —
   idempotent, verified on-device) and report whether the transport
   accepted it. With no live connection it must report not-responsive
   without attempting the transfer. Do not change the connection state
   machine or the standby/close behavior.

2. State surface (ModernWigiDash.Hardware): expose the latest probe
   verdict through the engine's existing public state surface so the App
   can observe it (the badge reads engine state). Do not change the
   meaning of `ConnectionState`.

3. App wiring (ModernWigiDash.App): run one probe per second from the
   existing 1-second telemetry cadence — the PollLoop shape the sensor
   and frame-time producers use (the loop tick runs on a background
   thread, so the probe call must not block the UI thread). Follow the
   existing loop shape; do not add new timer infrastructure to the
   window.

4. Tests (ModernWigiDash.Tests): MSTest unit tests that drive the probe
   through the engine's existing transport-factory seam (the internal
   test constructor that wires the factory to an injected transport):
   the live-connection accepted path, the live-connection refused path,
   and the no-connection path. Tests must not touch real USB.

5. Verification — both must be green before you call the task done:
   - `dotnet build ModernWigiDash.slnx -c Release --nologo` (0 errors)
   - the new test class passes:
     `dotnet test ModernWigiDash.slnx -c Release --nologo -p:BaseOutputPath=C:\Users\tobia\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\wmd-build\ -nodeReuse:false --filter "FullyQualifiedName~<YourTestClass>"`

Rules for this task:
- Do NOT commit, branch, tag, or revert anything. Leave your final state
  in the working tree, uncommitted, so the diff can be reviewed
  afterwards.
- Keep the change minimal: the probe, its state surface, the App wiring,
  and the tests. No new features beyond the probe.

When you finish, report:
- the files you changed and what each change does,
- the exact mechanism by which the probe avoids blocking the UI thread,
- the final build result and the filtered test result (verbatim last
  lines).
